subject: Human Body
title: Dopamine: Reward and Motivation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Dopamine: Reward and Motivation.

hook.text: Dopamine doesn't cause pleasure. It causes wanting. It drives you toward goals before you reach them.

buildup.text: In the brain's reward circuits, dopamine drives behavior: food seeking, learning, social bonding, and achievement.

discovery.text: Dopamine surges when a reward is unexpected. Predictable rewards produce less dopamine. Surprise drives the system.

climax.text: Dopamine is about anticipation, not satisfaction. It's the craving, not the pleasure.

punchline.text: Dopamine makes you want. It doesn't make you happy.

quiz.question: When does dopamine surge the most?
options: When a reward is unexpected or surprising
After completing a long task with no reward
